claim_scope: Direct non-interval scan for sign-changing positive-axis roots in lambda=[0.630,0.650]; not a global or certified no-fold theorem.
implementation: Python standard-library binary64; composite Simpson quadrature with 1200 panels; 200 t-subintervals; bisection; centered branch slopes only when the complete h=1e-5 stencil remains in 0<t<=1

endpoint_derivative.note: This replaces the invalid near-boundary binary64 centered-difference values. The canonical candidate remains HIGH_PRECISION, not a certified enclosure.

boundary_transversality_cross_check.binary64_simpson_local_ratios: approximately 1.10247 to 1.10250 across the sign change

observed_conclusion: Exactly one sign-changing positive-axis root was observed for every coarse lambda node from 0.630 through 0.643; none was observed from 0.644 through 0.650. Endpoint refinement shows that the branch approaches t=1 while the independently evaluated one-sided endpoint derivative stays finite and negative. No numerical signature of an interior fold was observed in the scanned window.
certification_gap: The scan cannot exclude an arbitrarily narrow unobserved root pair, and it says nothing about lambda outside [0.630,0.650]. A binding global no-fold result requires interval coverage proving partial_t g<0 on the branch region, sign/root exclusion on its complement, and a separate treatment of the unscanned lambda range.
audit_note: Project-owner audit on 2026-08-25 identified the invalid near-boundary centered stencil and supplied the converged one-sided dps=50 endpoint derivative sequence recorded above.
